extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent attorneys, and courts applying U.S. patent law (practitioners and litigants under the Patent Act of 1870)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and procedural/substantive standards from the Patent Act of 1870 governing patentability procedures, rights, remedies, fees, and related processes in the United States. Includes requirements for assignments, marking, caveats, reissue, appeals, extensions, design patents, and infringement defenses and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment in writing and recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent or any interest therein shall be assignable in law by an instrument in writing; assignments, grants, or conveyances shall be void as against any subsequent purchaser or mortgagee for a valuable consideration, without notice, unless it is recorded in the Patent Office within three months from the date thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 36. Assignments must be in writing and recorded within three months to be valid against subsequent purchasers without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior constructor's right
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, with the inventor's knowledge and consent, constructed, sold, or used a newly invented machine or other patentable article prior to the inventor's application shall have the right to use and vend the specific thing so made or purchased, without liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 37. Protects prior-constructed items made with inventor's consent from later liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to mark patented articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentees and their assigns or persons making or vending any patented article must give sufficient notice to the public that the same is patented, either by fixing thereon the word 'patented' with the day and year the patent was granted, or by fixing to it or its package a label containing like notice; failure to mark bars recovery of damages except on proof of actual notice of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 38. Marking is required to recover damages unless the defendant was duly notified and continued infringement after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition and penalty for false marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who marks upon any thing the name or imitation of the name of a patentee, or affixes the word 'patent' or similar words to an unpatented article with intent to deceive the public, shall be liable to a penalty of not less than one hundred dollars, recoverable by suit; one moiety to the suer and the other to the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 39. Criminal/civil penalty for fraudulent or deceptive marking; enforcement by district courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Any U.S. citizen desiring further time to mature an invention may file a caveat in the Patent Office setting forth its design and distinguishing characteristics; the caveat shall be confidential and operative for one year and gives the filer notice if a later application would interfere, allowing three months (plus mailing time) to file application materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 40. Caveats secure a one-year priority-like protection and trigger notice and limited opportunity to file if another application arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner must notify reasons for claim rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any claim for a patent is rejected for any reason whatever, the commissioner shall notify the applicant, giving him briefly the reasons for such rejection, together with such information and references as may be useful in judging of renewing his application or altering his specification; persistence shall prompt re-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 41. Rejection notice must include brief reasons and useful references; applicant's persistence leads to ordered re-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference/priority determination
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application would interfere with any pending application or unexpired patent, the commissioner shall notify the applicants and direct the primary examiner to determine priority of invention; the commissioner may issue a patent to the adjudged prior inventor unless adverse party appeals within prescribed time not less than twenty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 42. Formal interference/priority process with opportunities to appeal examiner decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for affidavits and depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner may establish rules for taking affidavits and depositions required in Patent Office cases; such affidavits and depositions may be taken before any officer authorized to take depositions to be used in U.S. courts or the State where the officer resides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 43. Commissioner-authorized procedural rules for testimonial evidence in PTO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena for witnesses for Patent Office cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerks of U.S. courts shall, upon application by any party or agent, issue a subpoena for any witness residing or being in their district to appear and testify before any officer authorized to take depositions for use in contested Patent Office cases; refusal may be enforced or punished by the issuing judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 44. Judicial assistance available to procure testimony for Patent Office contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness fees, travel limit, and secrecy protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses subpoenaed shall be allowed the same fees as U.S. court witnesses; no witness shall be required to attend more than forty miles from the place of service, nor be held in contempt for refusal unless fees and travel expenses and one day's attendance are paid or tendered at service; a witness may refuse to disclose any secret invention owned by himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 45. Limits on compulsory testimony and protections for witnesses regarding secret inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to examiners-in-chief after two rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicant for a patent or reissue whose claims have been twice rejected, and any party to an interference, may appeal from the decision of the primary examiner or the examiner in charge of interferences to the board of examiners-in-chief upon payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 46. Right to administrative appeal after two rejections or in interference cases (fee required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal appeal to commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with the decision of the examiners-in-chief may, on payment of the duty required by law, appeal to the commissioner in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 47. Further administrative appeal available to the commissioner personally (fee/payment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Supreme Court of the District of Columbia
rubrics_metrics.description: Except parties to an interference, a party dissatisfied with the commissioner's decision may appeal to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia sitting in banc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 48. Judicial appeal path from Commissioner to DC court for non-interference cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of reasons of appeal and notice when appealing to court
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is taken to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, the appellant shall give notice to the commissioner and file in the Patent Office, within such time as the commissioner shall appoint, his reasons of appeal, specifically set forth in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 49. Procedural requirement to file written and specific reasons of appeal within commissioner-prescribed time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's summary revision limited to appeal points
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall hear and determine the appeal and revise the decision appealed from in a summary way on the evidence produced before the commissioner, at such time as the court appoints; the revision shall be confined to the points set forth in the reasons of appeal; the court returns a certificate of its proceedings to be entered of record and governing further proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 50. Judicial review is summary and limited to specified appeal points; certificate governs Patent Office record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner to notify interested parties and furnish record
rubrics_metrics.description: On receiving notice of the time and place of hearing such appeal, the commissioner shall notify all parties who appear to be interested; the party appealing shall lay before the court certified copies of original papers and evidence, and the commissioner shall furnish the grounds of his decision fully set forth in writing; the commissioner and examiners may be examined under oath to explain principles of the invention on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 51. Duties to supply records, grounds, and permit examination of PTO personnel at court request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable remedy by bill in equity for refused application
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patent is refused by the commissioner or the Supreme Court of DC on appeal, the applicant may have remedy by bill in equity; the court may adjudge the applicant entitled to a patent as specified and authorize the commissioner to issue it upon filing a copy of the adjudication and complying with requisitions of law; if no opposing party, applicant pays all expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 52. Equity suit available to challenge refusals and obtain an order directing issuance; applicant may bear costs when uncontested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for inadvertent defects or over-claiming
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is inoperative or invalid due to a defective or insufficient specification, or because the patentee claimed more than his right, if the error arose by inadvertence, accident, or mistake without fraudulent intention, the commissioner shall, on surrender and payment of duty, cause a new patent to be issued in accordance with the corrected specification for the unexpired part of the term; specifications and claims shall be subject to revision and restriction as original applications; no new matter shall be introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 53. Reissue available for inadvertent errors; surrender and payment required; cannot add new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to specification/model rules for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: In reissue, for a machine patent the model or drawings shall not be amended except by each other; when neither model nor drawing exists, amendments may be made upon satisfactory proof that the new matter was part of the original invention and omitted by inadvertence, accident, or mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 53. Limits on amending models/drawings; new matter allowed only to correct inadvertent omissions with satisfactory proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer of over-claimed parts
rubrics_metrics.description: When through inadvertence a patentee has claimed more than he was the original inventor of, his patent shall be valid for what is truly his; such patentee may, on payment of duty, make disclaimer of parts he does not choose to claim, stating extent of his interest, attested and recorded, and it shall be considered part of the original specification to that extent; disclaimers do not affect pending actions except for unreasonable neglect or delay in filing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 54. Formal disclaimer procedure protects valid portions and must be recorded; timing can affect litigation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of courts and remedies (injunctions, damages)
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions arising under the patent laws shall be originally cognizable in equity as well as at law by circuit courts or district courts having circuit powers, or by the Supreme Court of DC; courts may grant injunctions according to equity principles and may award profits and damages, assessing and, in discretion, increasing damages as provided by this act; actions must be brought during the patent term or within six years after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 55. Broad federal jurisdiction for patent suits; injunction and damages remedies; statute of limitations tied to patent term or six years post-expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to writ of error or appeal to U.S. Supreme Court
rubrics_metrics.description: A writ of error or appeal to the Supreme Court of the United States shall lie from all judgments and decrees of any circuit court, district court exercising circuit jurisdiction, or Supreme Court of DC or Territory in any patent action, in the same manner as other judgments, without regard to the sum or value in controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 56. Final appellate route to the U.S. Supreme Court available for patent cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified Patent Office copies as competent evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Written or printed copies of any records, books, papers, or drawings belonging to the Patent Office, and of letters-patent under the commissioner's signature with the seal, shall be competent evidence where originals could be; certified copies of foreign patents' specifications and drawings shall be prima facie evidence of granting, date, and contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 57. Certification makes Patent Office records admissible as evidence; fee charged for certified copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief against interfering patents by equity suit
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are interfering patents, any person interested in one such patent or in the working of the invention may have relief against the interfering patentee by suit in equity; the court may adjudge either patent void in whole or part or inoperative or invalid in particular parts of the U.S., but judgments affect only the parties and those deriving title under them subsequent to rendition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 58. Equitable relief available to resolve interference conflicts; judgments have limited effect scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery and enhancement of damages for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages for infringement may be recovered by action on the case in federal courts in the name of the party interested, and whenever a verdict is rendered for the plaintiff the court may enter judgment for any sum above the actual damages found, not exceeding three times the amount of the verdict, together with costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 59. Courts may increase damages up to treble the verdict amount; costs awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innocent overclaim does not bar suit for bona fide part
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee innocently claimed to be original inventor of more than he was, he (or his representatives/assigns) may maintain suit for infringement of the part bona fide his own if it is a material and substantial part and definitely distinguishable; however, no costs shall be recovered unless a proper disclaimer has been entered at the Patent Office before suit, and not entitled if unreasonably neglected or delayed to enter disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 60. Protects enforcement rights for rightful portions of a patent even when other parts were erroneously claimed, but requires timely disclaimer to recover costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's special defenses in infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In any infringement action the defendant may plead the general issue and, with thirty days' written notice to the plaintiff or attorney, may prove special matters: (1) specification made to contain less or more than whole truth to deceive public; (2) surreptitiously or unjustly obtained patent for what was invented by another; (3) previously patented or described in printed publication prior to supposed invention; (4) not original and first inventor of any material and substantial part; (5) in public use or on sale in the country for more than two years before application or abandoned to the public. If any such matter is found for defendant, judgment rendered for him with costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 61. Enumerates five specific defenses (fraudulent specification, derivation, prior publication, lack of originality, prior public use/sale >2 years/abandonment) and notice/formal pleading requirements; same defenses available in equity suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content required for proving prior invention/use
rubrics_metrics.description: In notices as to proof of previous invention, knowledge, or use, the defendant shall state the names of patentees and the dates of their patents and when granted, and the names and residences of persons alleged to have invented or had prior knowledge, and where and by whom it had been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 61 (continuation). Specifies particulars that must be included in notices asserting prior art/usage defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign prior use or knowledge exception if good-faith belief
rubrics_metrics.description: If it appears that the patentee, at the time of his application, believed himself to be the original and first inventor, the patent shall not be held void on account of the invention or any part having been known or used in a foreign country before his discovery if it had not been patented or described in printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 62. Protects patentees who acted in good faith despite foreign prior knowledge absent prior patent/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for extension of patent term (timing & contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee desiring extension of a patent granted prior to March 2, 1861, shall apply in writing to the commissioner stating reasons and furnish an oathed written statement of the ascertained value of the invention and receipts and expenditures in sufficient detail to show loss and profit; application must be filed not more than six months nor less than ninety days before expiration and no extension shall be granted after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 63. Strict timing window and financial disclosure required for extension applications; no post-expiration extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice for extension application
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of an extension application and payment of duty, the commissioner shall publish notice in one Washington newspaper and other local papers deemed proper for at least sixty days prior to the hearing, stating the application and time/place for hearing so any person may appear and show cause why extension should not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 64. Public notice requirement to allow opposition to extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal examiner report on extension novelty/patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: On publication of notice of an extension application, the commissioner shall refer the case to the principal examiner of the relevant class, who shall report particularly whether the invention was new and patentable when the original patent was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 65. Examiner's factual/legal input on whether original patent was novel/patentable at grant time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting patent extension
rubrics_metrics.description: At the hearing the commissioner shall decide upon the evidence and, if satisfied that the patentee, without neglect or fault, has failed to obtain from the use and sale of his invention a reasonable remuneration for time, ingenuity, and expense bestowed and introduction into use, and that it is just and proper, having due regard to the public interest, the commissioner shall certify renewal and extend the patent seven years from expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 66. Extension criteria combine patentee's failure to obtain reasonable remuneration (without fault) and public-interest balancing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension benefits extend to assignees/grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: The benefit of the extension of a patent shall extend to the assignees and grantees of the right to use the thing patented to the extent of their interest therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 67. Extensions are effective for downstream holders to the extent of their rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fees schedule and specific charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates for patent fees: filing each original application $15; issuing each original patent $20; filing each caveat $10; application for reissue $30; filing each disclaimer $10; application for extension $50; granting each extension $50; appeal from primary examiners to examiners-in-chief $10; appeal from examiners-in-chief to commissioner $20; certified copies 10 cents per 100 words; recording assignments/agreements/powers of attorney: specified tiered fees; copies of drawings at reasonable cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 68. Enumerates monetary fees for a range of PTO services and filings (historical amounts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment locations and treasury handling of patent fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees may be paid to the commissioner, treasurer or assistant treasurers, designated depositaries, national banks, or receivers of public money designated by the Secretary of the Treasury, who shall give a receipt; all money received at the Patent Office shall be paid into the treasury without deduction; disbursements made by disbursing clerk of Interior Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 69. Prescribes authorized collectors, receipts, and required deposit of funds into U.S. Treasury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds for mistaken fee payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasurer of the United States is authorized to pay back any sums paid into the treasury as for fees accruing at the Patent Office through mistake upon certificate by the Commissioner of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 70. Procedure for refunding mistaken payments requires Commissioner's certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patents: eligibility and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has invented or produced any new and original design for a manufacture, pattern, impression, ornament, or new useful and original shape or configuration not known or used before and not patented or described in printed publication may, upon payment of duty and due proceedings as in inventions or discoveries, obtain a patent therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 71. Extends patentability to ornamental/shape designs with novelty and non-publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner may dispense with models for designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner may dispense with models of designs when the design can be sufficiently represented by drawings or photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 72. Flexibility for design patent filings where drawings/photos suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent term election
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs may be granted for the term of three years and six months, or for seven years, or for fourteen years, as the applicant may elect in his application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 73. Applicant chooses one of three statutory design patent term lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension for pre-1861 design patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentees of designs issued prior to March 2, 1861, shall be entitled to extension of their patents for seven years in the same manner and under the same restrictions as provided for extension of patents for inventions issued prior to that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 74. Transitional extension provision for older design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates of fees in design cases: for 3 years 6 months, $10; for 7 years, $15; for 14 years, $30; for other cases in which fees are required, same rates as inventions or discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 75. Specific fee amounts for elected design patent term lengths (historical).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of invention regulations to designs
rubrics_metrics.description: All regulations and provisions which apply to obtaining or protecting patents for inventions or discoveries, not inconsistent with this act, shall apply to patents for designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 76. General harmonization: design patents governed by same procedural rules unless inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal/transitional effect on pending applications and existing rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts and parts of acts cited are repealed but repeal shall not affect, impair, or take away any right existing under any of said laws; all actions and causes of action which have arisen under any of said laws may be commenced and prosecuted as though this act had not been passed, except remedial provisions of this act shall be applicable to suits hereafter commenced; applications pending at passage where duty paid shall be proceeded with as though filed after the passage of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 111. Transitional provisions preserve existing rights and provide for treatment of pending applications.
